_note:
Suspect counts are a ratchet, not a score: they may only stop growing. Two of these numbers are
explained rather than fixed, and both are recorded here because a number nobody can account for
gets --update'd blind.

(1) fil-PH 14: all fourteen are the same false positive -- a Han glossary term whose default is a
Latin brand name (B 站 -> "bilibili" 13 rows, 萌百 -> "Moegirlpedia" 1 row). That is the wording the
project intends to display in every locale that has no override: "bilibili" is the platform's own
name and appears in the English source string too. The rule fires because the term is Han and the
default is not Han, so it cannot tell "a translation leaked into this locale" from "the pinned
wording IS the brand name". Adding a fil-PH override equal to the default would satisfy the rule
while documenting nothing.

(2) ko-KR 31 (was 29): adding a 27th locale moves the cross-locale *median* length that the
length-outlier rule compares against, and two existing, untouched Korean rows crossed the 0.3x
threshold (eventsItems: 8 chars against a median of 21; costOnExceed: 7 against 20). Nothing in
ko-KR changed -- the median gained one more sample, and a length heuristic has no way to know that.
